l4-context/hint.ogg.spoken_text: The rock around a fossil is evidence too.

l4-hard-parts/question.ogg.text: Which parts are generally most likely to be preserved as fossils?
l4-hard-parts/question.ogg.spoken_text: Which parts are generally most likely to be preserved as fossils?

l4-hard-parts/l4-hard-parts-0.ogg.text: Hard parts such as teeth and bones
l4-hard-parts/l4-hard-parts-0.ogg.spoken_text: Hard parts such as teeth and bones

l4-hard-parts/explanation.ogg.text: Hard parts such as bones, teeth and shells are more likely to survive fossilisation than soft tissues. This makes the fossil record incomplete.
l4-hard-parts/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Hard parts such as bones, teeth and shells are more likely to survive fossilisation than soft tissues. This makes the fossil record incomplete.

l4-hard-parts/hint.ogg.text: Think about which materials are more durable after death.
l4-hard-parts/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Think about which materials are more durable after death.

l4-coprolite/explanation.ogg.text: A coprolite is fossilised poo. It can contain clues about ancient animals and their diets.
l4-coprolite/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: A coprolite is fossilised poo. It can contain clues about ancient animals and their diets.

l4-coprolite/hint.ogg.text: Some fossils preserve evidence of everyday activities.
l4-coprolite/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Some fossils preserve evidence of everyday activities.

l5-footprint-limit/question.ogg.text: A scientist finds one fossil footprint, with no bones nearby. Which conclusion is safest?
l5-footprint-limit/question.ogg.spoken_text: A scientist finds one fossil footprint, with no bones nearby. Which conclusion is safest?

l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-0..text: The exact species is always known
l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-0..spoken_text: The exact species is always known

l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-1..text: An animal left a track, but its exact species may be uncertain
l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-1..spoken_text: An animal left a track, but its exact species may be uncertain

l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-3..text: Its whole life story is known
l5-footprint-limit/l5-footprint-limit-3..spoken_text: Its whole life story is known

l5-footprint-limit/explanation.ogg.text: A footprint records an animal’s activity. Without more evidence, scientists may not be able to identify the exact species that made it.
l5-footprint-limit/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: A footprint records an animal’s activity. Without more evidence, scientists may not be able to identify the exact species that made it.

l5-footprint-limit/hint.ogg.text: Separate what the evidence shows from what it cannot show.
l5-footprint-limit/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Separate what the evidence shows from what it cannot show.

l5-colour-limit/question.ogg.text: Why can’t scientists usually work out skin colour from dinosaur bones alone?
l5-colour-limit/question.ogg.spoken_text: Why can’t scientists usually work out skin colour from dinosaur bones alone?

l5-colour-limit/l5-colour-limit-0.ogg.text: All dinosaurs were the same colour
l5-colour-limit/l5-colour-limit-0.ogg.spoken_text: All dinosaurs were the same colour

l5-colour-limit/l5-colour-limit-3.ogg.text: Bones usually lack the original skin pigment evidence
l5-colour-limit/l5-colour-limit-3.ogg.spoken_text: Bones usually lack the original skin pigment evidence

l5-colour-limit/explanation.ogg.text: Bones alone usually do not preserve skin colour. In rare fossils, special evidence such as preserved pigment structures can help researchers investigate colour.
l5-colour-limit/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Bones alone usually do not preserve skin colour. In rare fossils, special evidence such as preserved pigment structures can help researchers investigate colour.

l5-colour-limit/hint.ogg.text: Think about where an animal’s colour comes from.
l5-colour-limit/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Think about where an animal’s colour comes from.

l5-flight-limit/question.ogg.text: A dinosaur fossil has feathers. What can we conclude from that fact alone?
l5-flight-limit/question.ogg.spoken_text: A dinosaur fossil has feathers. What can we conclude from that fact alone?

l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-0.ogg.text: It had feathers, but it did not necessarily fly
l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-0.ogg.spoken_text: It had feathers, but it did not necessarily fly

l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-2.ogg.text: It was definitely a modern bird
l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-2.ogg.spoken_text: It was definitely a modern bird

l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-3.ogg.text: It could not have lived on land
l5-flight-limit/l5-flight-limit-3.ogg.spoken_text: It could not have lived on land

l5-flight-limit/explanation.ogg.text: Feathers existed in dinosaurs before the evolution of modern birds. Finding feathers alone does not prove that an animal could fly.
l5-flight-limit/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Feathers existed in dinosaurs before the evolution of modern birds. Finding feathers alone does not prove that an animal could fly.

l5-flight-limit/hint.ogg.text: A feature can have more than one use.
l5-flight-limit/hint.ogg.spoken_text: A feature can have more than one use.

l5-dimetrodon/question.ogg.text: Why is Dimetrodon excluded from the dinosaur group?
l5-dimetrodon/question.ogg.spoken_text: Why is Dimetrodon excluded from the dinosaur group?

l5-dimetrodon/l5-dimetrodon-2.ogg.text: It belonged to the separate synapsid lineage
l5-dimetrodon/l5-dimetrodon-2.ogg.spoken_text: It belonged to the separate synapsid lineage

l5-dimetrodon/l5-dimetrodon-3.ogg.text: It was another name for Spinosaurus
l5-dimetrodon/l5-dimetrodon-3.ogg.spoken_text: It was another name for Spinosaurus

l5-dimetrodon/explanation.ogg.text: Dimetrodon belonged to the synapsid lineage, the broader evolutionary group that also includes mammals. It lived before dinosaurs and was not one.
l5-dimetrodon/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Dimetrodon belonged to the synapsid lineage, the broader evolutionary group that also includes mammals. It lived before dinosaurs and was not one.

l5-dimetrodon/hint.ogg.text: Similar-looking back features do not prove close relationships.
l5-dimetrodon/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Similar-looking back features do not prove close relationships.

l5-marine-reptile/question.ogg.text: Which of these was an extinct marine reptile rather than a dinosaur?
l5-marine-reptile/question.ogg.spoken_text: Which of these was an extinct marine reptile rather than a dinosaur?

l5-marine-reptile/explanation.ogg.text: Ichthyosaurus was an ichthyosaur, a group of marine reptiles outside the dinosaur group. Living swimming birds are dinosaurs, so habitat alone is not enough to classify an animal.
l5-marine-reptile/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Ichthyosaurus was an ichthyosaur, a group of marine reptiles outside the dinosaur group. Living swimming birds are dinosaurs, so habitat alone is not enough to classify an animal.

l5-marine-reptile/hint.ogg.text: Use evolutionary groups rather than just where an animal lived.
l5-marine-reptile/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Use evolutionary groups rather than just where an animal lived.

l5-index-fossils/question.ogg.text: The same short-lived index fossil occurs in two rock layers far apart. What does this suggest?
l5-index-fossils/question.ogg.spoken_text: The same short-lived index fossil occurs in two rock layers far apart. What does this suggest?

l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-0.ogg.text: The rocks must have the same colour
l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-0.ogg.spoken_text: The rocks must have the same colour

l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-1.ogg.text: The rocks contain the same dinosaur species
l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-1.ogg.spoken_text: The rocks contain the same dinosaur species

l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-3.ogg.text: The layers formed at roughly the same time
l5-index-fossils/l5-index-fossils-3.ogg.spoken_text: The layers formed at roughly the same time

l5-index-fossils/explanation.ogg.text: Index fossils come from organisms that were widespread but existed for a relatively short geological time. They help scientists compare the ages of rock layers.
l5-index-fossils/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Index fossils come from organisms that were widespread but existed for a relatively short geological time. They help scientists compare the ages of rock layers.

l5-index-fossils/hint.ogg.text: Think about why a widespread fossil with a narrow time range is useful.
l5-index-fossils/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Think about why a widespread fossil with a narrow time range is useful.

l5-incomplete-record/question.ogg.text: Why does the fossil record give an incomplete picture of ancient life?
l5-incomplete-record/question.ogg.spoken_text: Why does the fossil record give an incomplete picture of ancient life?

l5-incomplete-record/l5-incomplete-recor.text: Many organisms decayed without becoming fossils
l5-incomplete-record/l5-incomplete-recor.spoken_text: Many organisms decayed without becoming fossils

l5-incomplete-record/l5-incomplete-recor.text: All fossils formed in one day
l5-incomplete-record/l5-incomplete-recor.spoken_text: All fossils formed in one day

l5-incomplete-record/explanation.ogg.text: Fossilisation requires suitable conditions. Many organisms decayed, and soft parts were especially unlikely to survive, so much evidence is missing.
l5-incomplete-record/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Fossilisation requires suitable conditions. Many organisms decayed, and soft parts were especially unlikely to survive, so much evidence is missing.

l5-incomplete-record/hint.ogg.text: Compare dying with being preserved: they are not the same event.
l5-incomplete-record/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Compare dying with being preserved: they are not the same event.

l5-bird-ancestry/question.ogg.text: Which statement best describes the relationship between birds and dinosaurs?
l5-bird-ancestry/question.ogg.spoken_text: Which statement best describes the relationship between birds and dinosaurs?

l5-bird-ancestry/explanation.ogg.text: Birds evolved within a branch of theropod dinosaurs. They are living dinosaurs, and pterosaurs were a separate reptile group.
l5-bird-ancestry/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Birds evolved within a branch of theropod dinosaurs. They are living dinosaurs, and pterosaurs were a separate reptile group.

l5-bird-ancestry/hint.ogg.text: Think about the branch that contains feathered dinosaurs.
l5-bird-ancestry/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Think about the branch that contains feathered dinosaurs.

l5-sail-evidence/question.ogg.text: A Spinosaurus fossil has tall back spines. Which claim is directly supported?
l5-sail-evidence/question.ogg.spoken_text: A Spinosaurus fossil has tall back spines. Which claim is directly supported?

l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-0.ogg.text: The sail was always bright red
l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-0.ogg.spoken_text: The sail was always bright red

l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-1.ogg.text: It had tall back spines; their exact function needs more evidence
l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-1.ogg.spoken_text: It had tall back spines; their exact function needs more evidence

l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-2.ogg.text: The sail acted exactly like a boat sail
l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-2.ogg.spoken_text: The sail acted exactly like a boat sail

l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-3.ogg.text: Every dinosaur had the same spines
l5-sail-evidence/l5-sail-evidence-3.ogg.spoken_text: Every dinosaur had the same spines

l5-sail-evidence/explanation.ogg.text: Tall back spines are an observed anatomical feature of Spinosaurus. Proposed functions of its sail-like structure need additional evidence and remain subjects of research.
l5-sail-evidence/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Tall back spines are an observed anatomical feature of Spinosaurus. Proposed functions of its sail-like structure need additional evidence and remain subjects of research.

l5-sail-evidence/hint.ogg.text: Distinguish a preserved structure from an explanation of its use.
l5-sail-evidence/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Distinguish a preserved structure from an explanation of its use.

l5-change-mind/question.ogg.text: What should scientists do when reliable new fossils challenge an old explanation?
l5-change-mind/question.ogg.spoken_text: What should scientists do when reliable new fossils challenge an old explanation?

l5-change-mind/l5-change-mind-3.ogg.text: Recheck and update the explanation using the evidence
l5-change-mind/l5-change-mind-3.ogg.spoken_text: Recheck and update the explanation using the evidence

l5-change-mind/explanation.ogg.text: Scientific explanations are tested against evidence. New fossils can lead researchers to revise ideas about dinosaur appearance, behaviour and relationships.
l5-change-mind/explanation.ogg.spoken_text: Scientific explanations are tested against evidence. New fossils can lead researchers to revise ideas about dinosaur appearance, behaviour and relationships.

l5-change-mind/hint.ogg.text: Good explanations must fit the available evidence.
l5-change-mind/hint.ogg.spoken_text: Good explanations must fit the available evidence.
